text:
Grace: hey team, first day and i'm blocked. internal service names (svc.internal) resolve to IPv6 (::ffff:10.70.4.6 or a straight AAAA) when i'm on split-tunnel WireGuard at home, but the VPN doesn't carry IPv6 so connections hang. office network works. Fedora 38 + NetworkManager. anyone run into IPv6-preferring DNS + split-tunnel weirdness?

Omar (Infra): welcome! yes, some resolvers or DNS64/NAT64 setups synthesize AAAA records and clients prefer IPv6, then if the tunnel provides only IPv4 you get a silent failure. quick checks: `getent ahosts svc.internal` and `curl -v -4 http://svc.internal` or `ping6 svc.internal`. also `resolvectl status` to see what DNS and routing systemd-resolved is using.

Grace: getent shows an AAAA then an A. `curl http://svc.internal` hangs, `curl -4 http://svc.internal` succeeds. `resolvectl status` shows our VPN DNS (10.200.4.2) but system prefers AAAA.

Lena (SRE): common fixes: 1) prefer IPv4 by updating /etc/gai.conf and uncommenting `precedence ::ffff:0:0/96  100` to prefer IPv4-mapped addresses, 2) add `AddressFamily inet` to your `~/.ssh/config` for ssh, 3) for systemd-resolved you can set `DNSOverTLS=false` and ensure the VPN DNS is first, but gai.conf is fastest. On Fedora you can also tell NetworkManager to set `ipv6.method=ignore` for the VPN connection if you don't need IPv6.

Omar (Infra): short-term onboarding workaround: use `curl -4` or `ssh -4` when you see hangs. Long-term we'll add a note to the new-hire network doc explaining AAAA/IPv6 preference and include the `gai.conf` and NetworkManager screenshots. Also consider adding a small script that detects if `getent ahosts <host>` returns an IPv6 first and tests `-4` connectivity automatically.

Grace: applied the gai.conf change and restarted network service; `curl http://svc.internal` works now and my onboarding tests pass. thanks!

Infra Bot: Created INF-873: "Onboarding: IPv6/AAAA preference causing split-tunnel failures + doc + detection" assigned to Networking.
